newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-SJOBERG AND VOELKER CLAIM MORE EUROPEAN RECORDS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SJOBERG AND VOELKER CLAIM MORE EUROPEAN RECORDS.

text.p: Sweden's Johanna Sjoberg and Germany's Sandra Voelker each claimed a second European record in two days at the European sprints and short-course swimming championships on Saturday.
Sjoberg, who set her first European short-course record in winning Friday's 50 butterfly, produced another outstanding swim to take the 100 butterfly crown.
The 18-year-old Swede narrowly led Voelker at the halfway mark but pulled away in the second half to win in 58.80 seconds.

The time eclipsed the 59.35 European mark set by East German Kornelia Gressler in this pool on December 21, 1985, and was not far from the 58.29 world mark posted by American Misty Hyman in Quebec City earlier this month.
Voelker, beaten into second place by Sjoberg in the 50 butterfly, had to settle for another silver, clocking 59.44.
But the 22-year-old German bounced back to win the 50 freestyle in 24.67, slicing 0.08 seconds from the European short-course record she shared with fellow German Franziska van Almsick.
On Friday Voelker had broken van Almsick's 100 freestyle European short-course mark.
Earlier Britain's Mark Foster, slowest qualifier in the heats, produced a determined swim in the final to win the men's 50 metres butterfly.
Foster clocked 23.91, outside his world best 23.45, but too good for nearest rivals Fabian Hieronimus of Germany (24.07) and Jonas Akesson of Sweden (24.25).
Susan Rolph clinched a second gold for Britain in the women's 100 individual medley.
Eight minutes after taking the silver behind Voelker in the 50 freestyle, Rolph returned to win the medley in 1:01.94, just 0.04 seconds ahead of fast-finishing Slovak Martina Moravcova.
Poland's Alicja Peczak, who served a two-year ban for steroid use, won the women's 200 metres breaststroke.
Peczak, third in Friday's 100 breaststroke, overhauled pacesetter Lena Eriksson of Sweden 50 metres from home and went away to win in 2:26.11 from Slovenia's Alenka Kejzar.
